ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The op-amp shown has a finite gain \( A = 1000 \) and an infinite input resistance. A step-voltage \( V_i = 1 \text{mV} \) is applied at the input at time \( t = 0 \) as shown. Assuming that the operational amplifier is not saturated, the time constant (in millisecond) of the output voltage \( V_o \) is _______.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the non-inverting terminal (+) of the operational amplifier is grounded; the input step voltage Vi is connected to the inverting-terminal node through a resistor labeled R = 1 kΩ; a capacitor labeled C = 1 μF is fed back from the output terminal Vo to this inverting-terminal node; inside the op-amp, the open-loop gain A = 1000 is marked. Reasoning: Let the voltage of the inverting input node be v_n. Since the non-inverting terminal is grounded, v_+ = 0; the op-amp is not saturated and the open-loop gain is finite, so v_o = A(v_+ - v_n) = -A v_n, therefore v_n = -v_o/A. The op-amp input resistance is infinite, and the input terminal does not absorb current. Write KCL for the inverting node: the current entering the node through the resistor is equal to the current through the feedback capacitor, namely (v_i - v_n)/R = C d(v_n - v_o)/dt. Substituting v_n = -v_o/A gives RC(A+1) d v_o/dt + v_o = -A v_i. Therefore the time constant of the output voltage is τ = RC(A+1). Substituting R = 1 kΩ, C = 1 μF, A = 1000: RC = 10^3 × 10^-6 = 10^-3 s = 1 ms, so τ = 1001 × 1 ms = 1001 ms.
